label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Subject: Re: Saturday alarm

Kristen,

It was my popcorn, and I’m sorry. On Saturday, November 7, at about 10:40, I put a bag in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button and went out front. A guy needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and helping him took longer than I thought, maybe six or seven minutes. By then the popcorn had burned and set off the alarm.

The store was cleared for about 25 minutes, and the engine from up on Hertel came out. There was no damage, just smoke and a terrible stink. This was on me, not the microwave. I should have stayed there and watched it.

I feel bad about the customers having to stand out in the cold, and about the Hendersons leaving their cart. I expect they’ll be back—they always are—but I know that doesn’t make it any better. I’ll buy Denise her coffee too.

I do want to clear up that the September alarm wasn’t me. That was the sensor in the paint aisle.

I’ll cover the $175 dispatch bill. You can take it out of my check or I can bring you cash, whichever you prefer.

One of the guys on the engine was Mikey Szymanski. I broke him in as a probie back in ’03, and he’s never going to let me forget this. Thirty-one years on the job and my first alarm as a civilian is over a bag of butter popcorn. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

I know I messed up, but I really hope I can keep my Saturday shifts. I like the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. It won’t happen again.

Walt
